title: The Alhambra
hook: the red palace of Granada, walls covered with the words, no victor but Allah

segments.voice: Yesterday: Samuel ibn Naghrela and the neighbors of al-Andalus, sharing cities and words alongside inequality and violence. Your line was: shared, and not simple.

Stand in a courtyard in Granada and look closely at the wall. What looks like lace from a few steps back turns out, up close, to be writing: Arabic letters carved into plaster, woven through vines and stars. Some of it is the Qur'an. Some is poetry, praising the very room you're standing in. And again and again, one short sentence, small enough to fit in a corner and patient enough to fill a palace. Wa la ghaliba illa Allah. There is no victor but God.
screen: `LACE THAT TURNS OUT TO BE WRITING.` → `QUR'AN, POETRY, AND ONE SENTENCE.` → `NO VICTOR BUT GOD.`

segments.voice: The Alhambra sits on a hill above Granada. Its name is said to mean the red one, for the color of its walls. It was the palace of the Nasrid rulers of Granada. By then their map had shrunk: the Christian kingdoms had taken city after city, and Granada was what remained. That makes the motto worth hearing twice. People tell a story about it. The dynasty's founder came home from a battle, and the crowd hailed him as the victor. His answer, so the story goes, was the sentence that would cover his family's palace: no victor but God. Nobody can confirm the scene, but the sentence is carved there for anyone to read. It isn't a verse of the Qur'an word for word, but it leans on one. In Pickthall's translation: "Victory cometh only from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise." A ruler writing that on his own walls says something odd for a ruler: the win is not mine; the throne answers to someone else. Then the craft. The writing doesn't sit on top of the decoration; it is the decoration. Letters climb, interlace, turn into borders. Geometry repeats without ending. Some poems speak in the room's own voice, as if the building were talking. A palace that keeps reminding its owners who owns it. No victor but Allah.
screen: `THE RED PALACE ON THE HILL.` · `A STORY ABOUT A VICTORY.` · `VICTORY COMETH ONLY FROM ALLAH.` · `THE WRITING IS THE DECORATION.` · then, large: `NO VICTOR BUT ALLAH.`

segments.voice: Picture a wall where one sentence is carved over and over among leaves and stars, until your eye stops seeing the pattern and starts reading it. Then bring to mind something you've won lately, a deadline met, an argument settled, a good day, and hold it lightly beside the sentence: no victor but God. If you pray, let those words rest on your breath; if you don't, notice how it feels to hold a win more loosely.
The Alhambra. The red palace of Granada, where Qur'an, poetry and one motto are carved into the walls: no victor but God. Today's word.
Your line: no victor but allah. A win held loosely is still a win. Day nine hundred forty-three.
